title: Safeguarded One-Time Admin Keys for Emergency Elevation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a tightly-controlled, fully auditable mechanism for issuing time-limited, one-use administrative credentials ("crisis keys") to support urgent operational needs. These keys must integrate with RBAC v2, require multi-party SSO-backed approval paths, be cryptographically ephemeral (single-use tokens tied to an HSM/KMS), and produce high-fidelity audit trails for post-incident review. Goal is to replace ad-hoc emergency elevation patterns with a repeatable, secure flow that minimizes blast radius and supports compliance requirements.
background: On-call and SRE teams occasionally need immediate elevated access to remediate high-severity incidents (failover, data migrations, emergency rollbacks). Current practices rely on temporary manual escalation, shared break-glass credentials, or ad-hoc vendor assistance. Those approaches are hard to audit and increase risk. This ticket defines a formal, productized approach for issuing ephemeral admin keys with guardrails and observability.
goals: (1) Provide a mechanism to issue one-time admin keys usable for a bounded window and single operation. (2) Require pre-approval via SSO workflow and multi-party acknowledgement for high-privilege scopes. (3) Ensure all requests/events are logged to audit logging system with immutable retention and export paths for compliance. (4) Integrate with RBAC v2 so keys inherit the least-privilege policy required for the operation.
non_goals: (1) Replacing planned role-based access reviews or long-term elevation workflows. (2) Building a second separate auth system — this must integrate with our SSO/SAML and existing identity provider. (3) Enabling unrestricted use of generated keys for service-to-service automation.
proposed_design: High level: a Crisis Elevation Service (CES) that coordinates approval, key generation, audit recording, and revocation. Flow: 1) Initiator opens a request via Console or API and selects the target resource and minimal scopes. 2) CES evaluates risk tier (based on scope/resource/CI metadata) and requires the appropriate approval pattern (auto-approve for low-risk; two approvers for high-risk). 3) Approvers authenticate via SSO and sign the approval. 4) After approvals, CES requests a single-use admin token from KMS/HSM-backed key broker; token is tied to request ID, TTL (default 15 minutes), and can be used only from approved CIDR or device posture. 5) Token issuance emits atomic audit events to the audit-log pipeline (immutable store + append-only feed). 6) Token is automatically revoked at TTL or immediately when the operator completes the designated operation. 7) Post-incident, the request and all associated telemetry are surfaced to the incident review dashboard.
access_flow_details:
- Request creation: include justification, linked incident ID, target resource, requested scopes, intended operation.
- Risk assessment: compute risk score using RBAC v2 metadata and proximity to production.
- Approval policy: low (auto within team lead), medium (one SRE + one team lead), high (two cross-functional approvers + security).
- Authentication: approvers must re-authenticate via SSO (SAML/SCIM) with step-up MFA.
- Constraints: token bound to single UID and single API call pattern where possible; OR bound to console session with strict CSRF protections.
- Revocation: immediate revoke API and KMS revoke path; CES also monitors for suspicious activity and will auto-revoke on anomalous events.
rbac_v2_integration:
- Map requested scopes to RBAC v2 roles and compute least-privilege projection.
- The issued token is scoped to the minimal role subset necessary for the approved operation.
- If RBAC v2 policy prevents required scope, CES surfaces an escalation path to temporarily open a narrow exception tied to this request id and expiry.
- All policy changes made for an emergency elevation must be recorded as transient and auto-reverted.
sso_and_saml_requirements:
- Leverage existing SSO provider (Okta/Google SAML) for identity assertions and step-up authentication.
- Approvals must be bound to the approver's SSO assertion and contain signature metadata so audit can validate who approved and when.
- SCIM mapping required to ensure team memberships and approver eligibility are current.
- For air-gapped/private customers, support a delegated approver gateway that proxies approvals into CES with mutual TLS.
crypto_and_key_management:
- Keys generated via KMS/HSM; tokens are ephemeral and wrapped with key encryption keys.
- Token material never stored in plaintext in CES logs.
- Use short-lived asymmetric signatures to bind the token to request ID and TTL.
- Support hardware-backed signing for high-risk issuances and optional attestation to satisfy compliance audits.
audit_and_logging:
- Emit structured events at every stage: request_created, approval_requested, approver_signed, token_issued, token_used (with API call reference), token_revoked, post_review_closed.
- Events must include request_id, approver_sso_id, approver_ip, device_posture, and policy_delta if any.
- Retention: immutable audit events retained for 7 years in cold archive for regulated customers and 90 days in hot store for operational needs.
- Provide export connectors to SIEM (Splunk, BigQuery) and support signed proofs for compliance review.
console_and_api_changes:
- Console: new 'Crisis Elevation' page under Security > Admin Controls, request wizard, approver chooser, live approval status.
- API: /v1/emergency-elevations endpoints: POST to create, GET for status, POST /approve to sign, POST /revoke. API requires mTLS and SSO token exchange.
- Notifications: integrations with PagerDuty and Slack with redacted details (no token material in chat).
telemetry_and_alerting:
- Metrics: requests/day, approvals/duration, issuance_latency, token_usage_success_rate, auto_revokes_triggered.
- Alerts: any token_use from non-approved CIDR, more than N ops within TTL, or token_used_by_unexpected_principal triggers immediate auto-revoke and P0 paging.
- Dashboard: per-customer and cross-customer views of active and recently-used crisis requests.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests for approval flow, RBAC mapping, and token lifecycle.
- Integration tests with SSO sandbox, KMS emulator, and audit pipeline.
- Chaos tests: ensure auto-revoke on KMS unavailability and that partial approvals cannot produce tokens.
- Security review and internal red-team exercise to validate attack surface (replay, forged approvals, privilege escalation).
- Smoke tests for Console UX and API contract compliance.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: internal beta for SRE/on-call only (2 weeks).
Phase 2: limited cross-functional beta with Security and a couple of product teams (4 weeks).
Phase 3: global rollout with telemetry gates and optional customer opt-in for managed customers (8 weeks).
Fallback: if key issuance is unreliable or audit fidelity drops, disable issuance and fall back to manual on-call playbook with increased monitoring.
runbooks_and_docs:
- New runbook: 'Use Crisis Keys' with steps for creating requests, approvers, and emergency revocation.
- Ops runbook for on-call: how to respond to an auto-revoke, how to retrieve audit evidence, and how to escalate to Security.
- Engineering doc: API spec, schema for audit events, SSO mapping guide, and KMS integration notes.
- Compliance pack: signed event export example and retention policy summary.
acceptance_criteria: Create and approve a crisis request end-to-end via Console and API with full audit trail recorded.
Issued tokens are single-use or bound to a single console session and automatically revoked after TTL.
RBAC v2 mapping produces least-privilege tokens for approved operations and transient policy patches auto-revert.
Approvals require SSO re-authentication and include approver signature metadata in audit logs.
Telemetric alerts fire on suspicious token usages and auto-revoke flow is verified in chaos testing.
implementation_tasks: Design CES API and database schema for request state and audit references.
Implement approval engine with SSO step-up integration and approver eligibility checks.
Integrate KMS/HSM token broker and implement single-use token bindings.
Emit structured audit events to existing pipeline and add SIEM connectors.
Console UI: build request wizard and approval status UI components.
Add telemetry and alerting rules in the observability stack.
Write runbooks, docs, and perform security review/red-team testing.
Create migration script for customers with legacy emergency procedures (optional opt-in).
